title: Multi-Objective Optimization of Trailing-Edge Flaps on the NREL 5 MW Wind Turbine for Power Enhancement and Blade-Root Load Mitigation
content: Designing trailing-edge flaps for utility-scale wind turbines requires balancing aerodynamic power extraction against blade-root loading. This study formulates the design of a trailing-edge flap on the NREL 5 MW rotor as a Pareto optimization of power coefficient and single-blade flapwise root moment at a prescribed steady operating point. To examine this trade-off, four flap variables: chord ratio, radial extent, radial position, and deflection were first sampled using a Latin-hypercube design and then optimized with NSGA-II. Selected points from the resulting Pareto front were recalculated with a refined NeuralFoil–BEM model that updates Reynolds and Mach numbers iteratively, and three representative designs were reconstructed independently in QBlade using XFOIL polars. A separate three-dimensional CFD calculation was then carried out for the Baseline and selected Win–win configuration. The search yielded 63 unique Pareto designs, ranging from cases that preserve power to solutions providing progressively greater root-moment relief. For the selected Win–win design, the refined model, QBlade, and CFD predict power-coefficient increases of 0.12%, 0.29%, and 0.31%, together with flapwise root-moment reductions of 6.39%, 6.06%, and 4.98%, respectively. A Practical-compromise design achieves approximately 12% root-moment reduction with a power penalty below 2% in the refined BEM and QBlade chains. Across all three aerodynamic models, the selected configuration consistently predicts a lower flapwise root moment while maintaining approximately the same power at the investigated operating point.
